projects.title: Clone Yourself
projects.description: A Chrome extension that deploys an autonomous AI agent into meetings on your behalf. It joins calls, listens, responds, and makes decisions in your voice and style, letting you be in multiple places at once. Built to handle low-to-mid value meetings without requiring your direct involvement.

projects.title: Sub $50 Gaze Prediction System (Entrepreneurs First Hackathon). "Computer Vision-Powered Eye Tracking with Ensemble Learning and Real-Time Inference Pipeline"
projects.description: Developed an affordable eye tracking system using dual webcam configuration and advanced computer vision techniques. Implemented pupil detection via dlib facial landmark recognition, MediaPipe iris tracking, and adaptive thresholding with contour detection. Built a machine learning pipeline using scikit-learn that generates polynomial features from eye coordinates and feeds them into a RandomForest regression model to accurately map eye movements to screen coordinates. Incorporated Kalman filtering for tracking stability and a historical buffer system for robust performance in varying lighting conditions.

projects.title: ASL Buddy (HackSheffield 2024 2x Winning Project)
projects.description: An award-winning iOS application that leverages cutting-edge computer vision to interpret American Sign Language (ASL) and gamifies learning through interactive quizzes. This project won the Top Sponsor Prize at HackSheffield 9 (sponsored by Frasers Group) and an additional prize from SWICS.

projects.title: Scholarly (DurHack 2024)
projects.description: A web application that eases scholarship discovery. Using advanced web scraping, it pushes scholarships into a centralized database. Users provide their details, and AI matches them with scholarships they are most likely to succeed in securing.

projects.title: Money Mentor (The Warwick Hackathon 2024)
projects.description: A financial literacy app that leverages OCR and computer vision to analyse receipts, providing users with actionable spending insights.The project was presented in front of judges from Capital One, Netcraft and the University of Warwick as part of The Warwick Hackathon 2024.

projects.title: Decipher
projects.description: A web app designed to explain python code to beginners starting out in their programming journey.Leverages Machine Learning through the OpenAI API to analyse and explain each line of code in plain, beginner friendly language.Platform uses a robust user authentication system with login and registration, enabling users to save and revisit previous code queries for continuous learning.

I thought finding a cofounder was mostly about chemistry. One week in San Francisco changed my mind. It’s been a wild first week. I watched a SpaceX launch, met some incredibly sharp people, and had conversations that completely shifted how I think about building. But the biggest thing I’ve been thinking about is this: Finding a cofounder is a lot like getting into a relationship. Chemistry matters, but chemistry alone is not enough. Complementary skills are not enough either. You can get along incredibly well with someone, and still be completely wrong for each other as cofounders. What matters first is whether you want to build toward the same future. Do you share the same level of ambition? Do you agree on what is worth spending the next 10 years chasing? Do you actually want to build the same kind of company? Then comes the second part: What is your edge? What is theirs? And when you put the two together, do those edges compound toward the same vision? That’s when the relationship starts to make sense. The other thing that has surprised me about SF is how willing people are to help. You can meet someone who has already built something huge, tell them you’re still at the beginning, and they’ll still give you their time. They’ll challenge your thinking, share what they learned, make an introduction, or point you in a better direction. There’s a ridiculous amount of ambition here, but also a ridiculous amount of generosity. One week down. Still learning, still testing ideas, still figuring out what is worth dedicating the next decade to. But I know why I came here. To build. For the founders here: What made you realize you’d found the right cofounder?

« Qui ne tente rien, n'a rien » 💫 {nothing ventured, nothing gained} Un mois à Sciences Po, sans raison particulière (ou presque) 🇫🇷 A month ago, I packed my bags for Paris, venturing on my first study abroad, leaving behind home comfort, exchanging it for a thirst of the unknown. I decided to go to the university, Sciences Po in Paris to study French intensively at B2-C1 level for a month. This involved writing and standard exam practice, alongside real world speaking experience, often in the form of social and historically contextual visits during our atelier {workshop} sessions. I decided to take part in this venture, purely because I believe each language we know gives us a different perspective on the world... « apprendre une nouvelle langue, c'est avoir une nouvelle âme » {to learn a new language, is to have a new soul}. Having taken French for so long before I came to university, it only felt like a natural step, and one that will allow me to later take the DALF C1 exam, signalling recognised proficiency / fluency, ideally within the next 3-6 months. As a Computer Science student, this was a wholly new domain, especially studying alongside and socialising with people who came mainly from a humanities / political science background, and it gave me new insights and ways of thinking I will take back with me. I am so glad that I partook in this course, deepening my level of the French language, and more importantly motivating me to keep it up in the future. To my 2 professors, Marie LeCocq and Assia M'Jalled, and to all the friends I made along the way - it was a pleasure to spend the month with you guys ‼️ Now the computer science lock-in resumes... 👀
